summary: This article explains how glaciers form from snow, flow slowly downhill, carve valleys, break into icebergs, store fresh water, and shrink as Earth warms.
introduce: Show the title “Glaciers: Rivers of Ice” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: to press something together so it takes up less space
broken pieces of rock, wood, or other things that are left or carried along
when large pieces of ice break off the edge of a glacier into water

challengeTerms.def: to gather or pile up little by little over time
the slow wearing away of land or rock by water, wind, or ice
a long pile of rocks and soil left behind by a glacier

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that glaciers far away from Saudi Arabia still matter to people who live here? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how glaciers help people and why melting glaciers are a problem.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review compress, debris, and calving, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses accumulate, erosion, and moraine to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
